text: Suppose molecular phylogenetics places ctenophores as the sister group to all other animals, with the non-neural sponges positioned closer to bilaterians. What is the most parsimonious implication for nervous system evolution?
choices: Nervous systems arose independently in ctenophores and in the ancestor of the remaining neural animals (polyphyly)
All animal nervous systems are homologous, descending from a single origin (monophyly)
Sponges must have secondarily lost a fully formed nervous system
Ctenophores must be derived descendants of cnidarians
explanation: If the neuron-less sponges branch between ctenophores and the other neural animals, the simplest reading is that neurons evolved twice, once in ctenophores and once in the cnidarian-plus-bilaterian lineage (polyphyly). Monophyly is the competing hypothesis this topology argues against; positing sponge loss of a nervous system is less parsimonious; and this topology places ctenophores basal to, not derived from, cnidarians.
